title: Hellfire Celebrational I
description: Welcome to the Hellfire Celebrational format! In this page, you can expect to see:
highlights: A quick overview of the format and why it exists;
The list of battle clauses in effect;
The list of banned held items;
The list of Pokémon you must use at least one of;
overview:
Hellfire Celebrational is a custom competitive format designed to celebrate Hellfire's current members and accomplishments at MirageCraft.
The main constraint of this format is the fact that all Pokémon may only use moves of their own type!

Type Restriction Clarifications

  • Pokémon that bring a Mega Stone are forced to Mega Evolve on turn 1 and may only use moves of the same type as their Mega Evolution. A Mega Staraptor may not use Normal-type moves.
  • Pokémon with abilities that change their typings, such as Color Change or Protean, or that get their typing changed by other Pokémon's moves, such as Soak, may only use moves of their originally allowed typings.
  • Pokémon with abilities that consider moves as being types other than the original may not use moves that were not originally of their types. A Mega Salamence with Aerilate may not use Double-Edge.

clauses.title: Endless Battle Clause
clauses.body:
Players cannot intentionally prevent an opponent from being able to end the game without forfeiting.

Example: A Slowbro can create an endless battle by having a Leppa Berry equipped and the moves Recycle, Heal Pulse, Slack Off and Block. You are not allowed to trap an opposing Pokémon and force an infinite battle by healing the opponent after PP stalling it.

clauses.title: Species-Form Clause
clauses.body:
Players cannot use two Pokémon that share the same Pokédex number and form in the same team, unless explicitly mentioned in the Pokémon table.

Players are allowed to use two of the same Pokémon if they use different forms (if the forms are allowed).
